title: Do we really need 8 hours’ sleep
titleChinese: 我们真的需要八小时睡眠吗？
paragraphs: Charles Darwin once said “A man who dares to waste one hour of time has not discovered the value of life”. If you live one hundred years, that only equates to twelve-hundred months – and when you break it down even further into days, hours and minutes, it gets more frightening. Why is this relevant? Well, quite simply put: life is short. Spending eight hours every day in a slumber means you’re losing a third of your life to bed. So, the question is: is eight hours the exact amount we need, or is it just a myth?

While most scientists agree that between seven and nine hours a night is the optimal amount, this is just a rough estimate. In truth, it’s a little more complicated than that. It seems that the amount of sleep you need depends upon your age – with infants needing much more than adults. What does seem apparent is that around seven and a half hours’ sleep is a good amount. In a study conducted at the University of Surrey Sleep Research Centre, the effects of sleep were monitored. One group slept for six and a half and the other for seven and a half hours per night. While some findings were predictable – irritation and lower concentration in the group who slept less, there were some more surprising findings. The genes of people who had less sleep were affected. Genes associated with inflammation, the immune system and stress response became more active. The team also observed increases in the activity of genes related to diabetes and risk of cancer.

One of the biggest issues is that myths regarding sleep are constantly perpetuated. For example, have you ever heard that you can train yourself to need less or no sleep? It’s simply not true. We will always need a certain amount of sleep – eight hours might not be the exact sweet spot, and there are factors like age to take into consideration, but one thing is true – there is a certain amount we do actually need.

vocabulary.entry: equate /ɪˈkweɪt/ v. 等同于；使相等
vocabulary.example: People often equate wealth with happiness.
vocabulary.translation: 人们常常把财富等同于幸福。

vocabulary.entry: slumber /ˈslʌmbə/ n. 睡眠；安眠
vocabulary.example: She fell into a deep slumber after a long day.
vocabulary.translation: 劳累了一天后，她沉沉睡去。

vocabulary.entry: myth /mɪθ/ n. 错误观念；荒诞说法
vocabulary.example: It’s a myth that eating carrots improves your eyesight instantly.
vocabulary.translation: 吃胡萝卜能立即改善视力是一种错误观念。

vocabulary.entry: optimal /ˈɒptɪməl/ adj. 最佳的；最适宜的
vocabulary.example: The optimal temperature for this plant is 20 degrees Celsius.
vocabulary.translation: 这种植物的最佳生长温度是20摄氏度。

vocabulary.entry: rough estimate /rʌf ˈestɪmət/ n. 粗略估算
vocabulary.example: The figure is just a rough estimate, not a precise calculation.
vocabulary.translation: 这个数字只是粗略估算，并非精确计算。

vocabulary.entry: infant /ˈɪnfənt/ n. 婴儿；幼儿
vocabulary.example: The infant was sleeping peacefully in its cot.
vocabulary.translation: 婴儿在婴儿床里安静地睡着。

vocabulary.entry: apparent /əˈpærənt/ adj. 显而易见的；明显的
vocabulary.example: It was apparent that she was upset by the news.
vocabulary.translation: 很明显，这个消息让她心烦意乱。

vocabulary.entry: conduct /kənˈdʌkt/ v. 实施；开展（研究等）
vocabulary.example: Researchers conducted a survey on public transport usage.
vocabulary.translation: 研究人员开展了一项关于公共交通使用情况的调查。

vocabulary.entry: monitor /ˈmɒnɪtə/ v. 监测；监控
vocabulary.example: Doctors monitored the patient's heart rate throughout the night.
vocabulary.translation: 医生整夜都在监测病人的心率。

vocabulary.entry: irritation /ˌɪrɪˈteɪʃn/ n. 易怒；烦躁
vocabulary.example: Lack of sleep can lead to irritation and mood swings.
vocabulary.translation: 睡眠不足会导致易怒和情绪波动。

vocabulary.entry: concentration /ˌkɒnsnˈtreɪʃn/ n. 注意力；专注力
vocabulary.example: The noise outside made it hard to maintain concentration.
vocabulary.translation: 外面的噪音让人难以集中注意力。

vocabulary.entry: gene /dʒiːn/ n. 基因
vocabulary.example: This gene is responsible for determining eye color.
vocabulary.translation: 这种基因负责决定眼睛的颜色。

vocabulary.entry: inflammation /ˌɪnfləˈmeɪʃn/ n. 炎症；发炎
vocabulary.example: The medicine helps to reduce inflammation in the joints.
vocabulary.translation: 这种药物有助于减轻关节炎症。

vocabulary.entry: immune system /ɪˈmjuːn ˈsɪstəm/ n. 免疫系统
vocabulary.example: A balanced diet can strengthen the immune system.
vocabulary.translation: 均衡饮食能增强免疫系统。

vocabulary.entry: stress response /stres rɪˈspɒns/ n. 应激反应
vocabulary.example: The body’s stress response helps it cope with dangerous situations.
vocabulary.translation: 身体的应激反应有助于应对危险情况。

vocabulary.entry: active /ˈæktɪv/ adj. 活跃的；活性的
vocabulary.example: The virus is still active in the body for several days.
vocabulary.translation: 这种病毒在体内仍会保持活性好几天。

vocabulary.entry: diabetes /ˌdaɪəˈbiːtiːz/ n. 糖尿病
vocabulary.example: He has to take insulin every day to control his diabetes.
vocabulary.translation: 他每天都得注射胰岛素来控制糖尿病。

vocabulary.entry: cancer /ˈkænsə/ n. 癌症
vocabulary.example: Early detection of cancer can improve the chances of recovery.
vocabulary.translation: 癌症的早期发现能提高康复几率。

vocabulary.entry: perpetuate /pəˈpetʃueɪt/ v. 使持续；使长存
vocabulary.example: These stories perpetuate the myth of a perfect society.
vocabulary.translation: 这些故事让完美社会的错误观念一直流传下去。

vocabulary.entry: train /treɪn/ v. 训练；培养
vocabulary.example: You can train your mind to stay calm under pressure.
vocabulary.translation: 你可以训练自己的大脑在压力下保持冷静。

vocabulary.entry: sweet spot /swiːt spɒt/ n. 理想状态；最佳点
vocabulary.example: The sweet spot for studying is in the morning when you’re alert.
vocabulary.translation: 早上头脑清醒的时候是学习的最佳时段。

vocabulary.entry: factor /ˈfæktə/ n. 因素；要素
vocabulary.example: Weather is a key factor in planning a picnic.
vocabulary.translation: 天气是策划野餐的关键因素。

vocabulary.entry: consideration /kənˌsɪdəˈreɪʃn/ n. 考虑；考量
vocabulary.example: Safety is our main consideration when designing the product.
vocabulary.translation: 安全性是我们设计这款产品时的首要考量。

vocabulary.entry: relevant /ˈreləvənt/ adj. 相关的；切题的
vocabulary.example: Please provide only relevant information for the report.
vocabulary.translation: 请只提供与报告相关的信息。

vocabulary.entry: break down /breɪk daʊn/ v. 分解；拆分
vocabulary.example: We need to break down the task into smaller steps.
vocabulary.translation: 我们需要把这个任务拆分成更小的步骤。

sentences.english: Charles Darwin once said “A man who dares to waste one hour of time has not discovered the value of life”.
sentences.chinese: 查尔斯·达尔文曾说过：“敢于浪费一小时时间的人，还没有发现生命的价值。”

sentences.english: If you live one hundred years, that only equates to twelve-hundred months – and when you break it down even further into days, hours and minutes, it gets more frightening.
sentences.chinese: 如果一个人能活一百年，那也只相当于一千二百个月——再进一步把它拆解成日、时、分，这个数字会更令人心惊。

sentences.english: Well, quite simply put: life is short.
Spending eight hours every day in a slumber means you’re losing a third of your life to bed.
sentences.chinese: 每天花八个小时睡觉，意味着你有三分之一的生命都在睡梦中度过。

sentences.english: So, the question is: is eight hours the exact amount we need, or is it just a myth?
sentences.chinese: 那么问题来了：八小时睡眠是我们所需的准确时长，还是只是一个固有说法？

sentences.english: While most scientists agree that between seven and nine hours a night is the optimal amount, this is just a rough estimate.
sentences.chinese: 尽管大多数科学家都认同每晚七到九小时是最佳睡眠时长，但这只是一个粗略的估算。

sentences.english: In truth, it’s a little more complicated than that.
sentences.chinese: 事实上，实际情况要比这复杂一些。

sentences.english: It seems that the amount of sleep you need depends upon your age – with infants needing much more than adults.
sentences.chinese: 一个人需要的睡眠时长似乎取决于年龄——婴儿需要的睡眠时间远多于成年人。

sentences.english: What does seem apparent is that around seven and a half hours’ sleep is a good amount.
sentences.chinese: 有一点似乎很明确：每晚大约七个半小时的睡眠是比较合适的。

sentences.english: In a study conducted at the University of Surrey Sleep Research Centre, the effects of sleep were monitored.
sentences.chinese: 萨里大学睡眠研究中心开展了一项研究，监测了睡眠带来的影响。

sentences.english: One group slept for six and a half and the other for seven and a half hours per night.
sentences.chinese: 研究人员将受试者分为两组，一组每晚睡六个半小时，另一组睡七个半小时。

sentences.english: While some findings were predictable – irritation and lower concentration in the group who slept less, there were some more surprising findings. The genes of people who had less sleep were affected.
sentences.chinese: 一些研究结果在意料之中——睡眠不足的一组出现了易怒、注意力下降的情况，但还有一些结果更令人惊讶：睡眠不足者的基因受到了影响。

sentences.english: Genes associated with inflammation, the immune system and stress response became more active.
sentences.chinese: 与炎症反应、免疫系统和应激反应相关的基因变得更加活跃。

sentences.english: The team also observed increases in the activity of genes related to diabetes and risk of cancer.
sentences.chinese: 研究团队还发现，与糖尿病和癌症风险相关的基因活性也有所上升。

sentences.english: One of the biggest issues is that myths regarding sleep are constantly perpetuated.
sentences.chinese: 关于睡眠的错误观念一直在被不断传播，这是最棘手的问题之一。

sentences.english: For example, have you ever heard that you can train yourself to need less or no sleep?
sentences.chinese: 比如，你有没有听过这种说法：你可以训练自己适应更少的睡眠，甚至不睡觉？

sentences.english: We will always need a certain amount of sleep – eight hours might not be the exact sweet spot, and there are factors like age to take into consideration, but one thing is true – there is a certain amount we do actually need.
sentences.chinese: 人类始终需要一定时长的睡眠——八小时或许并非精准的理想时长，而且还有年龄等因素需要考虑，但有一点是毋庸置疑的：我们确实需要充足的睡眠。
